verdicts.reason: The card's only axis is fleet $/GB from recovering stranded memory, and its own literature says a switch-based design loses money on that axis. Pond (ASPLOS '23) gets ~7% gross DRAM saving at 16 sockets (7-9% on the poster), from emulation on Azure traces, and uses an external memory controller specifically to avoid switch latency. Octopus (Azure plus universities, arXiv 2501.09020) finds CXL switches produce a net server-cost increase and only 3-5.4% net saving for the best switchless topology. Google's HotNets '23 'A Case Against CXL Memory Pooling' argues cabling and switching cost more than multiplexing saves (all via search snippet). For a 16-socket, 12 TB pod, 7-9% is ~$17-22k at the 4Q26 deck and ~$7-9k in the glut, before switch, controllers, cables and a 1-5% slowdown [ESTIMATE]. Mainline Linux (opened, 2026-10-31) still scores Dynamic Capacity, multi-host sharing and fabrics [0], so the dynamic reallocation the saving depends on is unsupported. C-76 was already killed as a duplicate of this card, so this verdict covers the pooling idea in both forms.

new_evidence.shows: (via search snippet) Reduces DRAM needs by 7% with a pool spanning 16 sockets; 8-16 sockets capture most of the benefit; emulation on Azure production servers.

new_evidence.title: Octopus: Scalable Low-Cost CXL Memory Pooling
new_evidence.shows: (via search snippet) In simulation, Octopus gives 3-5.4% net server cost savings, while CXL switches give a net cost increase.

new_evidence.title: A Case Against CXL Memory Pooling (HotNets '23)
new_evidence.shows: (via search snippet) Pooling's multiplexing savings are outweighed by the cost of the required cabling and switching, plus complexity and limited utility.

new_evidence.title: Linux CXL maturity map
new_evidence.shows: Opened via git sparse clone. Multi-host memory DCD [0], Sharing [0], Fabrics/G-FAM [0], Switch CCI [0], LD hotplug [1].
